recommendations.title: Incidence and intrinsic risk factors of hamstring strain injuries among Malaysian footballers: a cohort study of 81 professional footballers
recommendations.authors: Muhammad Y. Yunus; Ahmad H. Shushami; Alston Choong; Mohamad A. Azwan
recommendations.reason: Include: prospective cohort of Malaysian professional association footballers during the 2023 Malaysian Football League, with team physician/physiotherapist injury surveillance, time-loss hamstring strain outcomes, and direct exposure-hour denominators for total, match, and training incidence.
recommendations.dataCollectionTiming: Preseason assessments were followed by injury surveillance throughout the 2023 Malaysian Football League season.
recommendations.populationEligibility: 81 Malaysian professional male footballers from senior, U23, and U20 teams in a single professional club.
recommendations.competitionContext: 2023 Malaysian Football League season, including training and match exposure.
recommendations.dataSource: Team physician and/or team physiotherapist injury reports using FIFA F-MARC consensus injury data collection methods.
recommendations.outcomeEligibility: Hamstring strain injury incidence and severity/time-loss surveillance.
recommendations.injuryIllnessDefinition: Time-loss posterior-thigh strained-muscle injury, with severity classified by days absent from training and matches.
recommendations.reportedDenominator: Total exposure 24,147.5 h; match exposure 1,072.5 h; training exposure 23,075 h.
evidenceQuotes: This was a prospective cohort study of 81 Malaysian professional footballers
This study was conducted throughout 2023 Malaysian Football League.

Data collection was conducted based on the method proposed by the Injury Consensus Group, which was established under the Fédération Internationale de Football Association Medical Assessment and Research Centre
All injuries during training and competition reported by the footballers to either team physician and/or team physiotherapist, will be recorded
The injury incidence is reported as the number of injuries per 1000 player hours, including match and training injury incidence.
